title: Internal Controls — Evaluating the Severity of a Control Deficiency and Designing Remediation
scenario: Northstar Services reported revenue of $62,000,000 and pre-tax income of $6,200,000 for the year. Internal audit found that any sales representative can issue a credit memo against a customer account in the billing system with no supervisory approval and no link to a returned-goods or service-failure record. During the year the company issued 1,240 credit memos totaling $2,480,000, and internal audit determined that 465 of them carried no evidence of approval or supporting documentation. Management sets its planning materiality at 5% of pre-tax income. Answer each requirement in complete sentences and show your computations.

requirements.prompt: Requirement 1 — Compute the average credit memo, the dollar value of the unapproved memos, and the company's materiality threshold. Using magnitude and likelihood, evaluate whether this condition is a control deficiency, a significant deficiency, or a material weakness, and support your classification.

noneOf: this is only a minor deficiency

requirements.modelAnswer: The average credit memo is $2,480,000 spread over 1,240 memos, or $2,000. The 465 memos lacking approval therefore represent roughly $930,000 of revenue reversals, against a materiality threshold of 5% of $6,200,000 pre-tax income, which is $310,000. The unapproved population is three times that threshold. Severity turns on two factors: the magnitude of the misstatement the control could fail to prevent, and the likelihood that such a failure occurs. Magnitude is clearly material at $930,000, and likelihood is not merely theoretical, because 37.5% of all memos already went through without approval. When a deficiency creates a reasonable possibility of a material misstatement that will not be prevented or detected on a timely basis, this is a material weakness rather than a lesser finding, and it must be reported to the audit committee.

requirements.prompt: Requirement 2 — Identify which COSO components are implicated by this finding, recommend a remediation plan containing at least one preventive and one detective control, and describe how internal audit should confirm that the remediation is operating effectively.

anyOf: require approval before the memo posts
noneOf: a policy memo alone is sufficient

requirements.modelAnswer: The finding sits squarely in control activities, since the approval step simply does not exist, but it also implicates risk assessment, because nobody identified credit memos as a fraud-prone revenue reversal, and monitoring, because 465 exceptions accumulated unnoticed. The preventive fix is a system-enforced approval workflow: the billing system should block any memo above a set limit from posting until a supervisor outside the sales function approves it and a reason code plus supporting documentation is attached. The detective fix is a monthly exception report of memos by representative and by customer, reviewed by the controller, with unusual concentrations investigated. Internal audit should then retest after the remediation has run for a sufficient period, drawing a fresh sample from the post-implementation months, reperforming the approval check, and confirming that no memo posted without documented evidence.
